notes.author: Ravi Iyer
notes.text: Kickoff with Lorna Whitcombe. Replacing a homegrown WMS across all 14 DCs before peak season. Budget $2.8M. Dmitri Sokolov initially proposed switching all DCs over one long weekend in January.

notes.author: Sana Qureshi
notes.text: Built an integration dependency map: carrier rating APIs, 3 customer EDI feeds per DC on average, the labor management tool, and a yard system nobody on the current team owns. 61 interfaces total.

notes.author: Ravi Iyer
notes.text: Recommended wave rollout: pilot at the smallest DC (Beaumont), then 3 waves grouped by shared carrier integrations. Lorna agreed after seeing the dependency map. Hana Pruitt nominated floor supervisors as super-users per DC.

notes.author: Sana Qureshi
notes.text: Beaumont pilot live. Pick-rate dropped 22% for the first 5 days, then recovered to baseline by day 12. Found that the yard system silently depended on an old nightly file; would have broken all 14 DCs in a big-bang.

notes.author: Ravi Iyer
notes.text: Wave 1 (4 DCs) live with a 2-week parallel run on inventory counts. Super-user model is working: 80% of floor questions resolved without IT tickets.

notes.author: Sana Qureshi
notes.text: Wave 2 live. One EDI customer (a large grocer) rejected new ASN format; caught during parallel run, fixed before go-live of the next DC. Dmitri: "The map paid for itself three times."

notes.author: Ravi Iyer
notes.text: Final wave complete, 3 weeks ahead of revised plan. No shipment SLA breaches during rollout. Recommending close-out once hypercare ends.

simulation.lesson: In multi-site operational system replacements, starting with a small pilot site and then rolling out in waves grouped by shared integrations works better than a single cutover. Mapping every integration up front, including ones with no current owner, is what makes the waves safe, and a short parallel run on core records catches external-partner format issues before they spread.
simulation.why: A pilot site exposes silent dependencies cheaply; waves grouped by shared integrations prevent one hidden issue from breaking every site.
simulation.conditions: Multiple sites, many external partner integrations, peak-season operational risk.
simulation.scale: Multi-site rollout across a large network
